prompt: How do I recall a sent message in Outlook?
completion:
**Recalling a sent e‑mail in Outlook (desktop client, Exchange/Office 365)** > *Recall works only for messages sent from an Exchange/Office 365 mailbox to another Exchange mailbox that is accessed with Outlook. > If the recipient is on Gmail, a corporate IMAP account, Outlook on the web, or has already opened the message, the recall will fail or be ignored.* --- ## Step‑by‑step | Step | Action | Tips | |------|--------|------| | 1 | **Open Sent Items** | Find the folder that contains the e‑mail you want to recall. | | 2 | **Open the message** | Double‑click the message to open it in its own window (not the preview pane). | | 3 | **Go to the “Message” tab** | The ribbon should show “Message” (sometimes “Actions” is hidden in the “More Commands” dropdown). | | 4 | **Choose Recall** | • In older Outlooks (2010–2016):
 `Actions` → `Recall This Message…`
• In newer Outlook 365:
 `Message` → `Move` → `Actions` → `Recall This Message…`
• Or right‑click the message header → `Recall this message…` | | 5 | **Select your option** | • **Delete unread copies of this message** – removes the original if it hasn’t been read.
• **Delete unread copies and replace with a new message** – opens a new editor window so you can send a revised e‑mail. | | 6 | **Confirm** | Click **OK**. Outlook will send a recall request. | | 7 | **Check the recall status** | A dialog may appear for each recipient:
 • “Recall was successful”
 • “Recall failed – the message was already read”
 • “Recall failed – message was not sent by Exchange” | --- ## What happens after you send the recall request? | Scenario | Result | |----------|--------| | Recipient **has not opened** the message | Recall **succeeds** – the message disappears from their inbox. | | Recipient **has opened** the message | Recall **fails** – the original message remains, but you may still see a status notification. | | Recipient uses **Outlook Web App** or a **non‑Exchange** client | Recall **fails** – Outlook can’t remove the message. | | Recipient’s mailbox is **already full or has a server issue** | Recall may **fail** or be delayed. | > **Important:** A recall request is just a request sent to the Exchange server. The server checks whether the recipient’s mailbox still holds an unread copy. If the copy has already been read or moved, the recall is ignored. --- ## Common pitfalls & how to avoid them | Problem | Why it happens | What to do | |---------|----------------|------------| | “Recall not available” button is greyed out | You’re using Outlook for Mac, Outlook on the web, or a non‑Exchange account | Recall isn’t supported; consider sending a follow‑up message instead. | | Recall works only half the time | The recipient’s message has already opened or read the message | Time the recall as soon as possible, or ask the recipient to delete it manually. | | You see “Recall failed – message was not sent by Exchange” | The e‑mail was sent from a POP/IMAP account (e.g., Gmail, Yahoo) | Recall won’t work; you’ll need a different approach. | --- ## Alternatives if recall fails | Approach | How to do it | |----------|--------------| | **Send a corrected e‑mail** | Click **Replace** in the recall dialog, edit the message, and resend. | | **Ask the recipient to delete it** | Send a brief apology e‑mail: “I’d like to retract my previous message. Please delete it when you get a chance.” | | **Use a “Do‑not‑read” reminder** | Add a reminder or a “Please delete this” note in the body. | | **Use an e‑mail tracking add‑in** | Some add‑ins (e.g., *HubSpot Sales*, *Yesware*) let you see if a message was opened and can trigger a follow‑up if not read. | --- ## Quick cheat‑sheet 1. **Open Sent Items → Open the mail.** 2. **Ribbon → Message → Actions → Recall This Message.** 3. **Choose “Delete unread copies of this message”** (or “Replace”). 4. **Confirm → Wait for status notification.** If the recall button isn’t there, you’re probably on a platform that doesn’t support it (Mac, OWA, or a non‑Exchange account). In that case, the best next step is a polite follow‑up or a request to delete the message. --- ### TL;DR - **Recall** works only in Outlook on Windows with Exchange/Office 365 and if the recipient hasn’t read the mail yet. - Open the sent message → Message tab → Recall This Message → pick “Delete unread copies” or “Replace”. - If it fails, send a follow‑up or ask the recipient to delete it manually.
